newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank's Feldt says EMU requires ERM membership.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank's Feldt says EMU requires ERM membership.

text.p: The chairman of the board of Sweden's central bank said on Wednesday he believed Sweden would need to join the EU's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) to qualify for participation in the currency union of the European Monetary Union (EMU).
"We can't have a floating exchange rate right up until the day we merge with the Euro," board chairman and former finance minister Kjell-Olof Feldt told business daily Finanstidningen.
This stance contrasts with the position of Riksbank governor Urban Backstrom, who says it is up to Sweden itself to decide whether or not it wants to peg the crown in the ERM.
"The crown has to join some form of exchange rate mechanism sooner or later," Feldt said, adding that Sweden would need to find out how it should prepare for EMU membership.
Feldt said he believed Sweden should participate in currency union from its projected start.
"Sweden should aim to join from the beginning in 1999," he said.
